Grinnell Glacier from Mount Gould: 4 photographs, 71 years, one viewpoint

1938
1981
1998
2009
T. J. Hileman · Glacier National Park Archives, 1938
Carl Key · U.S. Geological Survey, 1981
Dan Fagre · U.S. Geological Survey, 1998
Lindsey Bengtson · U.S. Geological Survey, 2009

Grinnell Glacier, photographed from the summit of Mount Gould in 1938 by T. J. Hileman. Ice fills the floor of the basin below the cliff. There is no lake.

43 years later, the same view from the same summit. A lake has opened at the foot of the ice, with slabs of it floating in the water.

17 years later, the same view from the same summit. The lake has widened, and the ice that feeds it has drawn back up the slope.

11 years after that, and 71 after the first frame. The basin is a lake with ice floating on it. What is left of the glacier hangs on the shelf above.

Repeat photography of Grinnell Glacier, Glacier National Park, Montana. T. J. Hileman, Carl Key, Dan Fagre, Lindsey Bengtson — Glacier National Park Archives and the U.S. Geological Survey; all 4 in the public domain. Each frame centre-cropped to one common aspect and resampled to 820×1215; nothing else was changed. Every original's own URL and sha256 is in photographs.csv beside this beat.
